subject: Latency vs Cost: Hyperscaler probe & cache/batch sensitivity
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Cole <emma@acme.ai>, James Li <james.li@verticloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Latency vs Cost: Hyperscaler probe & cache/batch sensitivity

Thanks for the time this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps from our side.

What we heard from VertiCloud and what matters to Acme:
- VertiCloud claim: lower per-token price on the managed endpoint but with limited batching controls and no customer-visible KV cache behavior.
- Acme needs: predictable 95th pct latency (<120ms for inference requests), predictable unit economics (per-1M tokens), and visibility into cache hit impact on cost.

Redwood differentiators we discussed:
- Intelligent batching + latency SLO routing so you can hit latency targets while still getting batching benefits.
- Prefix/KV cache that materially reduces token generation for multi-turn flows (we see 30–70% token savings depending on conversation reuse).
- Quantization and kernel selection that improves GPU efficiency without major quality regressions.

Proposed probe (we want to align before starting technical work):
1) 1M-token run per test cell. Each cell will run 1M output tokens across the same model variant and requests. Cells:
   a) Batch sizes: 1 / 8 / 32
   b) Cache hit profiles: simulated 20% / 60% / 90% hit rates
   c) Measure: cost per 1M tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, token-level billing breakdown (generation vs prompt).
2) One run against VertiCloud-managed endpoint (customer test account you provide) and one run against Redwood hosted/dedicated config.
3) Expected targets to validate: Redwood expects to be 25–55% lower on per-1M token cost in high-batch / high-cache scenarios, while staying within your p95 latency constraint. For conservative planning use: Redwood ~$1.10 / 1M tokens, VertiCloud ~$2.40 / 1M tokens (these are starting estimates — pilot will confirm).

Attachments: I attached a short TCO sweep worksheet and the detailed test plan (batch-cache-sensitivity-plan.pdf).

Ask / next steps:
- Emma/James: can you confirm a VertiCloud test endpoint and a sample traffic profile (qps, typical prompt length)? Emma mentioned she'd share an example QPS curve.
- Acme: confirm p95 latency SLO (we noted <120ms) and whether you need the pilot inside your VPC (private deployment) or whether a hosted/dedicated run is sufficient to validate economics.
- Internally: Ben + Rishi, please draft the exact metric collection and dashboard we will hand to Acme. Laura, are there any procurement/contract asks we need before we touch their test account?

Thanks — I can kick off test harnessing once we have the VertiCloud endpoint and qps file.

— Hannah

Thanks, Hannah — this looks good. Quick answers:
- I've attached our QPS curve (acme-qps-profile.csv) and a short example of prompt lengths.
- We can create a VertiCloud test endpoint — I will loop James on the exact account details.
- We prefer the pilot to run from within our VPC (data controls) if Redwood can support the Private deployment test; otherwise a hosted/dedicated run is OK for an initial economics readout.
- Confirming our p95 latency target: 120ms across normal traffic, 200ms acceptable for heavy tail if clearly documented.

Two asks from Acme before starting:
1) A one-page data access summary for our security team showing what logs/keys your platform will touch during the VPC run.
2) Estimated timeline and a preliminary quote for the pilot (cost to run the test harness + any reserved capacity we might need).

Happy to sync in a short call if needed; otherwise please send the security summary and timelines and we'll greenlight the VertiCloud test endpoint.

— Emma

Agree with the test matrix. A few practical notes from ops/pricing: 
- Price bands: to be conservative for Acme, plan for a 20% uplift on the pilot quote to cover burst capacity and dedicated slot reservation.
- Metrics: add GPU mem/compute utilization and per-request kernel selection tag so we can correlate cost deltas to execution path.
- Canary option: if Acme wants VPC, we should run a short canary (10k tokens) in their VPC first to validate networking and KMS flows before full 1M runs. That will surface any side-channel billing surprises.

I can draft the pilot quote and a one-page security summary for Emma. Assignments: I’ll own the pilot quote; Rishi can own the harness tech (metric collection + dashboard). Laura, loop legal for the VPC test addendum.

Decisions / owners: 
- Acme will provision a VertiCloud test endpoint and share credentials: Emma (owner) — expected by 2028-03-24.
- Pilot type: VPC canary (10k tokens) followed by full 1M token runs across 9 cells (3 batch sizes x 3 cache hit profiles). Redwood will support the VPC canary.
- Deliverables:
  * Ben: pilot quote + one-page security summary (due 2028-03-23 EOD).
  * Rishi: test harness + metric dashboard template (initial version due 2028-03-27).
  * Hannah: test coordination and final run sign-off; will own communications with Acme and VertiCloud.

Acceptance criteria (pilot):
- p95 latency <= 120ms for normal traffic, documented tail behavior for heavy load.
- Per-1M token cost report with line items (prompt tokens, generation tokens, infra amortization).
- Dashboard with cache-hit sensitivity curves and a recommended runbook for production rollout if Redwood proves economic.
